hero.headline: Trump names housing official Bill Pulte as acting intelligence chief
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who resigned last month. The appointment has drawn sharp criticism from both Democrats and Republicans, with concerns centered on Pulte's lack of relevant experience for the role.

Pulte, heir to a home construction company fortune, previously had no government experience before Trump appointed him to lead the FHFA, which oversees federal housing lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. He has no known background in national security or intelligence matters. Despite this, Trump stated on his Truth Social platform that "William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America." Pulte will continue serving as FHFA director while taking on the intelligence role.

Since arriving at the FHFA, Pulte has used his position to make public allegations against Trump's political opponents. He has accused Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of committing mortgage fraud, claims Cook has denied. This pattern of behavior has raised concerns among Republicans about potential weaponization of the intelligence apparatus.

Senate Republicans have expressed unease with the selection. John Thune, the Senate majority leader, told reporters that "we don't need a weaponized" national intelligence director. He noted that if Pulte is nominated for a permanent position, "he'll have to go through a confirmation process and hearings and everything else." Thune added: "We need professionals there."

As an acting appointee, Pulte can serve in the role without Senate confirmation. However, a permanent appointment would require Senate approval, a hurdle that may prove difficult given Republican reservations.

Gabbard's time in the position was tumultuous, with the former diplomat largely sidelined as Trump pursued aggressive policies toward Venezuela and Iran. According to two people briefed on the discussions, Trump had been asking cabinet members as early as April whether he should replace her.

Critics have highlighted Pulte's questionable handling of mortgage fraud allegations. One former high-ranking official described his approach in the Cook case as "very bizarre." A former Republican now working in media derided Pulte as a "nepo baby" with zero experience in military, intelligence, or government service.

The Pulte Family Charitable Foundation, which had ties to his family, publicly distanced itself from him in a 2023 statement, saying some of his communications had created confusion and emphasizing he does not represent their organization. The New York Times reported that Pulte no longer has any official connection to PulteGroup, having been pushed off the board in 2020.

The appointment comes as the intelligence community faces significant global security challenges, from counterterrorism operations to monitoring foreign adversaries.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio outlines U.S. demands as Iran negotiations stall
cards.teaser: The top U.S. diplomat detailed American conditions for peace during testimony as talks with Iran showed signs of faltering.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio presented U.S. demands during Senate testimony as diplomatic negotiations with Iran faltered. Iran has halted talks with the United States over Israeli military operations in Lebanon and Gaza.

Rubio's hearing addressed multiple foreign policy priorities including Taiwan and Cuba. Senator Jeanne Shaheen criticized the State Department for insufficient transparency on foreign policy matters. The testimony underscored ongoing tensions between the administration and lawmakers seeking greater congressional oversight of diplomatic efforts.

cards.headline: US Military Strikes Iranian Oil Tanker After Crew Ignores Warnings
cards.teaser: The US military fired a missile at an Iran-bound oil tanker, hitting the engine room after repeated warnings were ignored.
cards.body:
The US military fired a missile at an oil tanker bound for Iran, hitting the vessel's engine room. According to military officials, the crew had received multiple warnings before the strike was carried out as an enforcement action.

The incident occurred in the Strait of Hormuz region, where American aircraft have conducted several operations targeting Iranian interests and alleged smuggling vessels.

cards.headline: Trump scraps proposed $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.body:
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced on Tuesday that the Trump administration is abandoning its $1.8 billion fund designed to compensate individuals who claimed to be victims of government investigations. During a House appropriations committee hearing, Blanche stated clearly, "We are not moving forward with the fund, period."

The fund faced mounting legal and political obstacles since its announcement two weeks earlier. A federal judge in Virginia temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund after the nonprofit Democracy Forward filed a lawsuit challenging it. The decision to scrap the program marks a significant retreat on a proposal that had generated intense controversy across both parties.

Blanche explained the administration's rationale for the fund, saying, "The reasons for the fund is something that President Trump talked about for a long time, which is the fact that there were a lot of people in this country who had their government weaponized against them." However, he emphasized that moving forward with the fund was no longer viable.

The proposal had drawn criticism from multiple directions. Republicans including Senate Majority Leader John Thune expressed concern about lack of oversight and the possibility of payments to participants in the January 6, 2021 Capitol riot. Mike Pence, Trump's first-term vice president, called the prospect of compensating rioters "deeply offensive."

Democrats had vowed to force votes blocking the fund and launched investigations into it. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "the most brazen act of self-dealing yet and one of the most corrupt schemes ever launched by a president." Several Democratic-led states, including California, New York, Illinois, and Connecticut, proposed 100 percent income taxes on any distributions from the fund.

The fund was established as part of a settlement in Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service over the leak of his tax returns. The secretive nature of the fund, combined with the lack of transparency about who would receive payments and how much they would get, fueled accusations of corruption.

Despite scrapping the fund, Blanche confirmed that one significant element of the settlement remains in place. The administration is maintaining an agreement that prohibits the IRS from auditing Trump, his family, and related entities. The Justice Department had not defended itself in the original lawsuit against Trump, raising accusations among critics about collusion between the administration and the agency it controls through appointees.

The cancellation removes a major flashpoint between the Trump administration and Congress, though questions about executive power and financial accountability continue to dominate discussions on Capitol Hill.

cards.headline: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin declines to commit to following court orders
cards.teaser: The DHS chief faced Senate questioning about whether the department would comply with judicial rulings.
cards.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin appeared before the Senate Appropriations subcommittee to discuss the department's budget but drew attention for refusing to commit to following court orders. His testimony came amid airport security threats and protests over detention policies. Lawmakers pressed Mullin on whether DHS would comply with judicial decisions, but he did not provide a clear commitment.

Senators also accused Mullin of misrepresenting information about the Homeland Security budget during the hearing. The testimony occurred as the department faces scrutiny over its operations and as Republicans negotiate budget reconciliation legislation. Mullin's evasiveness on court compliance raised concerns among senators about executive branch respect for judicial authority.

cards.headline: Treasury Sanctions Iran's Largest Cryptocurrency Exchange
cards.body:
The U.S. Treasury Department has imposed sanctions on Iran's largest digital asset exchange, accusing the platform of facilitating terror financing and helping the Iranian government bypass international sanctions. The action targets the exchange for its connections to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and its role in moving funds that support Iranian military and proxy operations.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the United States seized approximately one billion dollars in Iranian cryptocurrency as part of the sanctions enforcement. The seizure represents one of the largest confiscations of digital assets tied to a foreign government and demonstrates the Treasury Department's intensifying focus on cryptocurrency platforms used to circumvent financial restrictions.

The sanctions prevent American individuals and companies from conducting transactions with the exchange and freeze any assets the platform holds within U.S. jurisdiction. Treasury officials described the exchange as a critical financial node for Iran, enabling the government to convert sanctioned funds into usable currency through digital asset trading. Officials stated that the platform processed transactions for entities previously designated for supporting terrorism and weapons proliferation.

Bessent characterized Iran as facing significant financial strain, citing the cryptocurrency seizure as evidence of the regime's reliance on alternative financial channels. According to Bessent's statements, Iran is "negotiating on fumes" regarding current discussions with the United States.

The sanctions action reflects growing U.S. government concern about cryptocurrency use by sanctioned governments and organizations. Digital assets provide a mechanism for moving money across borders without traditional banking infrastructure, making them attractive to countries isolated from the international financial system. The Treasury Department has expanded its capacity to track and seize cryptocurrency in recent years, working with blockchain analysis firms and international law enforcement to identify and freeze digital wallets connected to sanctioned entities.

This action comes amid ongoing tensions between the United States and Iran, including recent military exchanges near the Strait of Hormuz. The Treasury Department's sanctions announcement underscores the administration's strategy of maintaining economic pressure while pursuing diplomatic engagement. The timing reflects broader efforts to restrict Iran's financial capabilities across multiple channels.

Recent developments include military strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and apparent retaliatory actions by Iranian forces. These incidents highlight the tensions surrounding the waterway, which remains a critical shipping lane. Discussion regarding the strait's control and management has become a point of contention in ongoing negotiations between the two nations.

The cryptocurrency seizure represents a significant escalation in the Treasury's enforcement efforts against sanctioned entities using digital assets to evade restrictions. As the U.S. government continues developing tools to monitor blockchain transactions, cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset platforms face increasing scrutiny from regulators worldwide.

cards.headline: Six States Sue Trump Administration Over Offshore Wind Deal
cards.teaser: State attorneys general filed a lawsuit challenging a $1 billion payment to cancel a wind farm project.
cards.body:
Six states, led by New York's attorney general, filed a lawsuit challenging a Trump administration deal that paid a French company $1 billion to cancel an offshore wind project. The states argue the agreement violated environmental and procurement laws and failed to follow required procedures for terminating major renewable energy initiatives.

The lawsuit contends the administration acted improperly in negotiating the cancellation payment. According to the states, the deal undermines clean energy goals and wastes taxpayer money on scrapping offshore wind farms that were already in development.

hero.headline: UK Police Face Scrutiny After Student Dies From Stab Wound While Handcuffed
hero.body:
British authorities are investigating police officers who handcuffed a dying student, Henry Nowak, in a case that has sparked widespread public outrage and political debate. Nowak died from a stab wound while restrained by police, according to footage that has raised serious questions about police conduct.

Prime Minister addressed the case, stating that the arrest footage raises serious questions for police. The case has become increasingly politicized as public pressure mounts on law enforcement officials to explain why a critically injured person was handcuffed while dying. The investigation centers on whether officers followed proper protocols when responding to the incident.

The case has fueled broader tensions about policing practices in the United Kingdom. Political figures across the spectrum have seized on the incident, with some using it to criticize current law enforcement policies. The public response has been marked by anger and demands for accountability from the officers involved.

The circumstances surrounding how Nowak sustained his fatal stab wound and the timeline of police involvement remain under investigation. Authorities have not released complete details about what led to the decision to handcuff Nowak or how long he remained restrained before receiving medical attention.

The case has intensified existing debates about police use of force and treatment of individuals in distress. As the investigation continues, pressure grows on police leadership and government officials to provide answers about the incident and to implement reforms that could prevent similar deaths in the future.

cards.headline: Israel Continues Strikes in Southern Lebanon as Peace Talks Resume in Washington
cards.teaser: Israeli forces struck southern Lebanon as officials from Lebanon and Israel met in Washington for renewed peace negotiations.
cards.body:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has pledged to continue Israel's military operations against Hezbollah while Lebanese and Israeli officials hold peace talks in Washington. Following a U.S.-brokered deal, Israel has refrained from striking Beirut, though it maintains active operations in southern Lebanon.

The partial truce between Israel and Hezbollah has held in some areas despite ongoing Israeli military activity. Meanwhile, Iran has halted talks with the U.S., citing Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: US Court Delays Ebola Quarantine Unit Plans in Kenya
cards.teaser: A court ruling has further delayed Trump administration plans for a quarantine unit in Kenya meant for Americans exposed to Ebola.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has issued another ruling delaying the Trump administration's proposed quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola. The facility would have been located at Laikipia Air Base in Nanyuki, about 120 miles from Nairobi.

The plan has faced strong opposition from Kenyans living near the proposed site. Residents fear the facility will expose them to the virus, particularly since Kenya has no known Ebola cases. Local officials argue that quarantines should occur in citizens' home countries rather than in Kenya, viewing the proposal as a double standard applied by the United States.

cards.headline: Treasury Sanctions Iranian Cryptocurrency Exchange Nobitex
cards.teaser: The US Treasury imposed sanctions on Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange and several executives for helping evade sanctions.
cards.body:
The US Treasury Department sanctioned Nobitex, Iran's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, along with several of its executives. The Treasury accused the platform of helping the Iranian government evade existing sanctions and finance militant groups.

The action targets a key financial tool that Iranian authorities have used to work around international restrictions. By sanctioning the exchange and its leadership, the Treasury aims to close off avenues Iran has used to move money outside traditional banking channels that are already subject to US sanctions.

cards.headline: Trump Names Housing Official Bill Pulte as Acting Intelligence Director
cards.teaser: The head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency will step in as acting Director of National Intelligence.
cards.body:
Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, has been appointed as acting Director of National Intelligence. Pulte will oversee the nation's intelligence agencies despite lacking a traditional intelligence background.

During his tenure at the Federal Housing Finance Agency, Pulte advocated for criminal charges against individuals he identified as Trump's political opponents.

cards.headline: Protests Expand in Albania Over Kushner-Linked Resort Development
cards.teaser: Plans for luxury resorts on Albania's Adriatic coast have become a flashpoint for public frustration with the government.
cards.body:
Growing protests have erupted in Albania over plans for luxury resort developments on the Adriatic Sea linked to Kushner interests. The projects have long worried environmentalists concerned about coastal preservation and development impact.

The resort plans have evolved into a broader flashpoint for public frustration with the Albanian government. What began as environmental opposition has expanded to encompass wider grievances about government policies and development priorities in the coastal region.

The appointment represents Trump's approach of prioritizing loyalty in key national security positions, departing from the traditional practice of selecting intelligence directors with extensive military, intelligence, or national security backgrounds.

cards.headline: Six states hold midterm primary elections
cards.teaser: California, Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, and two other states conducted primary voting for November midterm races.
cards.body:
Voters in California, Iowa, New Jersey, South Dakota, New Mexico, and Montana cast ballots in midterm primary elections Tuesday, selecting candidates for the November general election. California's primary featured particularly competitive races for governor, Los Angeles mayor, and congressional seats.

California's vote-counting process is expected to move slowly, with county elections offices handling a surge of last-minute absentee ballots. Voting experts anticipate weeks of detailed ballot verification before final results emerge from the state's tightest races.

cards.headline: Federal investigators probe George Santos for insider trading on prediction market
cards.teaser: The Justice Department is examining whether the former congressman illegally bet on his own State of the Union attendance.
cards.body:
The Department of Justice is investigating former Representative George Santos for potential insider trading on Kalshi, a prediction market platform. Authorities are examining whether Santos placed bets on his own attendance at the State of the Union address, allegedly using information not available to the public.

Santos was expelled from Congress following revelations about fabricated background claims and campaign finance violations. The investigation centers on whether betting on outcomes he could directly control or had inside knowledge of constitutes illegal insider trading.

cards.headline: Senator Fetterman criticizes Senate candidate Platner over sexting reports
cards.teaser: The Pennsylvania senator called the Democratic candidate a creep following revelations of extramarital explicit messages.
cards.body: Senator John Fetterman called Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner a creep after reports emerged of sexually explicit texts Platner sent outside his marriage. The Wall Street Journal reported that Platner's wife had flagged the messages to his Senate

cards.headline: MSC Container Ship Hit by Projectiles at Iraqi Port
cards.teaser: A vessel owned by Mediterranean Shipping Company was struck by two projectiles while docked in Iraq.
cards.body:
A container ship owned by the Mediterranean Shipping Company was attacked by two projectiles at an Iraqi port, according to reports. The incident caused damage to the vessel but no immediate reports of casualties have been released.

The attack highlights ongoing risks to commercial shipping in the region even as the United States and Iran work to negotiate the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The strait has been partially closed due to regional tensions, disrupting major shipping routes and raising concerns about the safety of vessels operating in waters near Iran and Iraq.

cards.headline: Colorado Tightens Oversight of Uber and Lyft Operations
cards.teaser: A new law increases scrutiny of ride-hailing companies following reports of unreported sexual assault cases.
cards.body:
Colorado enacted legislation that increases regulatory scrutiny of Uber and Lyft operations in the state. The law was prompted by a New York Times investigation that found Uber received reports of sexual assault or sexual misconduct far more frequently than the company had publicly disclosed.

The new requirements will impose additional reporting and safety obligations on ride-hailing companies operating in Colorado. The legislation aims to improve transparency around passenger safety incidents and strengthen oversight of how companies respond to assault reports.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Shares Hit Record High on Strong Sales
cards.teaser: The lingerie retailer's stock surged 50 percent after reporting improved performance and raising annual forecasts.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret shares reached a record high after the company reported strong sales growth and raised its annual earnings forecast. The stock jumped 50 percent in its best single-day performance ever, driven by improved bra sales and successful turnaround efforts.

The retailer credited better product design and inventory management for the improved results. The company has worked to refresh its brand image and product line after years of declining sales. The upbeat forecast signals confidence that the turnaround strategy is gaining traction with customers.

cards.headline: Microsoft Announces More Reliable Quantum Computing Chip
cards.teaser: The company says its new quantum chip is 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor.
cards.body:
Microsoft unveiled its next-generation quantum chip, Majorana 2, which the company claims is 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor. The advancement represents progress toward making quantum computers practical for real-world applications.

The tech giant projects it will develop a quantum computer capable of solving commercially useful problems by the end of the decade. Quantum computers operate on different principles than traditional computers and could potentially tackle certain complex problems much faster, though the technology remains in early development.

cards.headline: Ulta Beauty Raises Earnings Outlook After Beating Expectations
cards.teaser: The beauty retailer reported stronger than expected sales and increased its full-year earnings forecast.
cards.body:
Ulta Beauty reported quarterly earnings that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year earnings outlook. The beauty retailer's shares jumped following the announcement, reflecting investor confidence in the company's performance.

The results showed growth across multiple product categories and sales channels. The company said beauty product purchases remained resilient despite broader economic concerns. The raised forecast suggests Ulta expects continued strong demand for cosmetics and personal care products throughout the year.

hero.headline: Microsoft unveils Scout AI assistant designed to encourage constant use
hero.body:
Microsoft announced Scout, a new AI assistant intended to function as an always-on personal agent, according to internal documents obtained by 404 Media. The documents reveal that the company wants to make people addicted to the assistant, which works like an executive assistant and never logs off.

The launch of Scout represents a major push by Microsoft into autonomous AI agents. The system is built on a technology platform called OpenClaw and is designed to handle tasks continuously without user intervention. Microsoft also announced Project Solara, a version of Android designed around agents rather than traditional applications, signaling a strategic shift in how the company envisions users interacting with their devices.

The announcement came during the Microsoft Build 2026 developer conference, where the company made several AI-focused reveals. Microsoft also unveiled new AI models intended to reduce its dependence on OpenAI and lower costs for developers. The company introduced an open-source Intelligent Terminal that integrates AI assistance directly into command-line workflows, and announced GitHub Copilot as a standalone desktop application designed for agent-native experiences.

Additionally, Microsoft announced WSL 3, which brings near-native GPU and NPU passthrough capabilities to Windows, enabling local AI processing. The updates position Windows as what Microsoft calls a trusted platform for development in an era the company describes as AI-driven devices.

The Scout assistant is designed to remain active and accessible at all times, functioning as what Microsoft describes as an AI coworker. The internal documents indicating the company's goal to create user addiction raise questions about the boundaries between helpful automation and dependency-driven product design. Microsoft has not publicly addressed the language used in the internal materials.

cards.headline: Cybersecurity firm Cyera seeks $12 billion valuation in new funding round
cards.teaser: The company is nearing a $300 million investment led by Evolution Equity Partners at 80 times its annual recurring revenue.
cards.body:
Cyera, a cybersecurity company, is close to securing a $300 million funding round that would value the firm at $12 billion. Evolution Equity Partners is leading the investment, which represents a valuation multiple of 80 times the company's annual recurring revenue.

The high valuation comes despite the company currently operating at a loss. The funding round reflects continued investor appetite for cybersecurity technology even at premium valuations relative to revenue.

cards.headline: Uber limits employee AI tool spending after exhausting budget in four months
cards.teaser: The company imposed caps after staff used AI resources more heavily than anticipated following encouragement to adopt the technology.
cards.body:
Rewrite

Uber has capped employee spending on AI tools after depleting its budget within four months. The rapid expenditure followed the company's push encouraging staff to maximize their use of artificial intelligence applications.

The spending limits represent a significant shift from Uber's initial strategy of promoting broad AI adoption across its workforce. The situation underscores the substantial costs companies encounter when scaling AI tool access without implementing usage constraints.

cards.headline: Lawsuit claims Ring cameras scan faces of guests and passersby without consent
cards.teaser: Legal action against the Amazon-owned company alleges facial recognition technology is applied to people captured on Ring devices.
cards.body:
A lawsuit filed against Ring, owned by Amazon, alleges the company scans the faces of visitors and people passing by homes equipped with its cameras. The complaint states Ring uses artificial intelligence to identify faces captured by the devices.

The lawsuit argues Ring should compensate Americans whose faces have been scanned by the technology. The legal action raises questions about consent and privacy when facial recognition systems operate on private property but capture images of people in semi-public spaces like sidewalks and driveways.

cards.headline: DIY cyberdeck computers gain popularity as alternative to mainstream tech
cards.teaser: Communities building custom portable computers from scratch have grown rapidly in recent months on social media.
cards.body:
Cyberdeck communities have experienced a surge in popularity over recent months, with people constructing their own portable computers and sharing designs on social media. The movement involves building devices like solar-powered game emulators, pocket-sized e-readers, and clamshell computers that fit in purses.

The trend represents a rejection of mainstream technology and corporate surveillance, with builders emphasizing style and functional substance. The growth in these DIY hardware communities reflects increasing interest in custom-built alternatives to mass-market consumer electronics, particularly among younger technology enthusiasts seeking more control over their devices.

cards.headline: YouTube TV subscribers offered 50 percent discount on Google TV Streamer
cards.teaser: Google is providing the promotional pricing on its streaming hardware device to current YouTube TV customers.
cards.body:
YouTube TV subscribers can purchase the Google TV Streamer at half the regular price through a promotional offer from Google. The discount applies to the company's streaming hardware device.

The promotion targets existing YouTube TV customers, bundling hardware savings with the subscription service. Google has not specified how long the offer will remain available.

cards.headline: Neanderthals used rhino teeth as hammers, research finds
cards.teaser: Archaeological analysis reveals ancient humans incorporated unusual materials into their tool collections.
cards.body:
Neanderthals included rhinoceros teeth among their tools, using them as hammers, according to archaeological research. The discovery adds to understanding of the range of materials ancient humans employed for practical purposes.

The finding shows Neanderthals adapted available resources in unexpected ways. Researchers identified the rhino tooth tools through analysis of archaeological remains from Neanderthal sites.

hero.headline: Curry signs $400 million endorsement deal with Li-Ning
hero.body:
Warriors superstar Stephen Curry has signed a 10-year endorsement contract with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning worth $400 million, according to sources. The deal marks one of the largest endorsement agreements in basketball history and represents a major shift in the global athletic footwear landscape.

The contract moves Curry away from his previous partnership with Under Armour, where he had been a signature athlete for years. Li-Ning, founded by Chinese Olympic gymnast Li Ning in 1990, has been expanding its presence in international basketball markets and seeking high-profile endorsers to compete with Nike, Adidas, and other established brands.

Curry's decision to partner with Li-Ning comes as Chinese sportswear companies have increased their investment in NBA talent. The $40 million annual average makes this one of the most lucrative athlete endorsement deals across all sports. For comparison, the contract puts Curry among the top earners in sports marketing, reflecting both his on-court success and global marketability.

The four-time NBA champion and two-time MVP remains one of basketball's most recognizable figures worldwide. His popularity in China has been particularly strong, with the Warriors regularly drawing massive television audiences during their games. Li-Ning likely views Curry as a centerpiece for its strategy to gain market share both in China and internationally.

The deal underscores the growing financial power of Chinese sportswear manufacturers in the global athletics industry. Li-Ning has previously signed deals with other NBA players but never at this scale. The company's stock has shown strong performance in recent years as it has modernized its brand image and expanded beyond the Chinese domestic market. For Curry, the partnership provides financial security well beyond his playing career while giving him a platform to expand his business interests in Asian markets.

cards.headline: Falcons extend Drake London with $141 million contract
cards.teaser: The Falcons and star wide receiver Drake London agreed to a four-year, $141 million contract extension.
cards.body:
The Atlanta Falcons and star wide receiver Drake London have agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $141 million, according to his agent Andrew Kessler. The deal locks in one of the team's top offensive weapons for the coming years.

The agreement reflects London's importance to Atlanta's passing attack and underscores the premium value top receivers command in today's NFL market.

cards.headline: Steelers sign Nick Herbig to $100 million extension
cards.teaser: Linebacker Nick Herbig agreed to a four-year, $100 million extension with the Steelers after sitting out minicamp drills.
cards.body:
Steelers linebacker Nick Herbig has agreed to a four-year, $100 million contract extension with $42 million guaranteed. The deal comes after Herbig sat out individual drills during the team's mandatory minicamp on Tuesday.

The extension resolves the contract dispute and allows Herbig to return to full participation with the team as it prepares for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Eagles teammates react to A.J. Brown trade departure
cards.teaser: Former Eagles teammates expressed mixed reactions to receiver A.J. Brown's trade, ranging from loss to relief.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation surrounding the three-time Pro Bowl selection. The deal reunites Brown with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel and sends the Eagles a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027.

Brown's departure drew mixed reactions from his former teammates. While some expressed a sense of loss at losing the talented receiver, others felt relief that the situation had finally been resolved. An Eagles left tackle captured the sentiment, telling reporters "Thank God it's over," reflecting how the ongoing saga had created tension within the locker room.

cards.headline: Browns required Jared Verse in Myles Garrett trade talks
cards.teaser: Browns general manager Andrew Berry said he would not have considered trading Myles Garrett without Jared Verse being included.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card:

The Cleveland Browns traded star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a blockbuster deal, acquiring linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection who set the single-season sacks record with 23 in 2025.

Browns general manager Andrew Berry revealed that Verse's inclusion was crucial to making the deal happen. Berry stated he did not seriously consider trading Garrett until the Rams added Verse to the proposal, underscoring the substantial compensation the franchise required to part with one of the league's premier defensive players.

cards.headline: Liverpool agrees to hire Andoni Iraola as head coach
cards.teaser: Liverpool reached an agreement to appoint Andoni Iraola as their new head coach, sources confirmed.
cards.body:
Liverpool have agreed a deal in principle with Andoni Iraola to become their new head coach, succeeding Arne Slot who was sacked on Saturday. The Spaniard will sign a two-year contract at Anfield following swift negotiations with the club's sporting director Richard Hughes.

Iraola's backroom staff will also move to Liverpool, with assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper joining him at the club.

cards.headline: Stanley Cup Final between Hurricanes and Golden Knights begins
cards.teaser: The NHL's Stanley Cup Final between the Carolina Hurricanes and Vegas Golden Knights starts with game one.
cards.body: The 2026 Stanley Cup Final begins on Tuesday with the Carolina Hurricanes facing the Vegas Golden Knights. Both teams have advanced through multiple playoff rounds to reach the championship series, where they will compete in a best-of-seven format to determine the Stanley Cup winner.

hero.headline: Matt Brown of 'Alaskan Bush People' Found Dead in Washington River at 43
hero.teaser: The reality television star's body was recovered from a river in Washington state.
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a star of the Discovery Channel reality series "Alaskan Bush People," has died at 43. His body was found in a river in Washington state, according to multiple reports.

Brown's brother Noah Brown stated the family is coming to terms with the death. The family has described their response as torn between grief and relief, though the circumstances leading to that characterization were not detailed in available reports. Matt Brown appeared on the reality show that followed his family's life in remote Alaska.

cards.headline: R&B Singer Peabo Bryson Dies at 75
cards.teaser: Peabo Bryson, the R&B singer known for his work on Disney film soundtracks, has died at 75, according to a statement from his family.
cards.body:
Peabo Bryson, the veteran R&B singer known for performing Disney's biggest film hits, has died at 75. His family announced his passing but did not provide a cause of death.

Bryson achieved his greatest fame as the voice behind "Beauty and the Beast" and "A Whole New World" from "Aladdin." These iconic songs became defining tracks of Disney's acclaimed animated films during the 1990s, introducing his smooth vocal style to audiences across generations worldwide.

cards.headline: Amazon Cancels Stargate Series From Martin Gero
cards.teaser: The streaming service has ended development on the planned television series that received a series order in November.
cards.body:
Amazon has canceled its planned Stargate television series, according to sources. The show received a series order in November 2025 and was set to be written and executive produced by Martin Gero, who served as showrunner.

Gero previously worked as a writer on "Stargate SG-1" and "Stargate: Atlantis" early in his career. The cancellation means the new series will not move forward at the streaming platform. Amazon has not publicly commented on the decision to end the project.

cards.headline: Zendaya and Tom Holland Stopped Production to Rewrite Spider-Man Scene
cards.teaser: The two actors spoke up on set when a scene was not working, leading the director to send the crew home for rewrites.
cards.body:
Tom Holland said on Amy Poehler's podcast that working with partner Zendaya provides a lifeline and he could not imagine doing his job without her. The two stars have appeared together in four Spider-Man films, including this summer's "Brand New Day."

During production on the latest film, both actors identified a scene that was not working. The director responded by sending the crew home so the scene could be rewritten. Holland described Zendaya as essential to his work, and the two will also appear together in an upcoming Christopher Nolan film.

cards.headline: Ben Folds Warns National Symphony Orchestra Faces Survival Crisis
cards.teaser: The musician and former artistic adviser outlined challenges facing the orchestra in an open letter.
cards.body:
Ben Folds has issued an open letter warning that the National Symphony Orchestra may not survive what he described as chaos at the Kennedy Center. Folds, who previously served as artistic adviser to the NSO, outlined the challenges currently facing the orchestra.

The letter also included information about what supporters can do to help the orchestra during this period. Folds connected the orchestra's difficulties to the Kennedy Center's current situation, though specific details about the nature of the challenges were not provided in the letter.

cards.headline: Insomniac Games Confirms Mature Rating for Wolverine Video Game
cards.teaser: The studio released new gameplay footage and confirmed the game will feature significant violence and a low-gore option.
cards.body:
Insomniac Games unveiled new gameplay footage for "Marvel's Wolverine" and confirmed the title will receive a mature rating. Creative director Marcus Smith emphasized the studio's commitment to delivering a mature experience, with the footage demonstrating the level of violence central to the game.

The developers discussed combat mechanics featuring Wolverine's claws, potential X-Men character appearances, and how the protagonist can die during gameplay. Players seeking a less graphic experience will have access to a reduced gore option.

cards.headline: Martin Scorsese Used AI to Storyboard Upcoming Film
cards.teaser: The director has partnered with an AI company and used its image-generation tool in pre-production.
cards.body:
Martin Scorsese has become an adviser and partner to Black Forest Labs, an AI company that develops image-generation tools. The acclaimed director used the company's Flux tool to help storyboard his next film during pre-production.

Scorsese's involvement marks a significant moment in Hollywood's adoption of AI technology. Rather than using the tool broadly, the director focused specifically on storyboarding, demonstrating a measured approach to incorporating artificial intelligence into his creative process.

hero.headline: Trump names housing official Bill Pulte as acting intelligence chief
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who resigned last month. The appointment has drawn sharp criticism from both Democrats and Republicans, with concerns centered on Pulte's lack of relevant experience for the role.

Pulte, heir to a home construction company fortune, previously had no government experience before Trump appointed him to lead the FHFA, which oversees federal housing lenders Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. He has no known background in national security or intelligence matters. Despite this, Trump stated on his Truth Social platform that "William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America." Pulte will continue serving as FHFA director while taking on the intelligence role.

Since arriving at the FHFA, Pulte has used his position to make public allegations against Trump's political opponents. He has accused Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of committing mortgage fraud, claims Cook has denied. This pattern of behavior has raised concerns among Republicans about potential weaponization of the intelligence apparatus.

Senate Republicans have expressed unease with the selection. John Thune, the Senate majority leader, told reporters that "we don't need a weaponized" national intelligence director. He noted that if Pulte is nominated for a permanent position, "he'll have to go through a confirmation process and hearings and everything else." Thune added: "We need professionals there."

As an acting appointee, Pulte can serve in the role without Senate confirmation. However, a permanent appointment would require Senate approval, a hurdle that may prove difficult given Republican reservations.

Gabbard's time in the position was tumultuous, with the former diplomat largely sidelined as Trump pursued aggressive policies toward Venezuela and Iran. According to two people briefed on the discussions, Trump had been asking cabinet members as early as April whether he should replace her.

Critics have highlighted Pulte's questionable handling of mortgage fraud allegations. One former high-ranking official described his approach in the Cook case as "very bizarre." A former Republican now working in media derided Pulte as a "nepo baby" with zero experience in military, intelligence, or government service.

The Pulte Family Charitable Foundation, which had ties to his family, publicly distanced itself from him in a 2023 statement, saying some of his communications had created confusion and emphasizing he does not represent their organization. The New York Times reported that Pulte no longer has any official connection to PulteGroup, having been pushed off the board in 2020.

The appointment comes as the intelligence community faces significant global security challenges, from counterterrorism operations to monitoring foreign adversaries.

cards.headline: Pentagon hires convicted Jan. 6 rioter for counterterrorism office
cards.teaser: The Defense Department appointed a man convicted for his role in the Capitol attack to work in its special operations office.
cards.body:
The Trump administration hired Elias Irizarry, who was convicted for participating in the Jan. 6, 2021 attack on the U.S. Capitol, to a position within the Defense Department's Special Operations and Low Intensity Conflict office. Irizarry was 19 years old when he took part in the Capitol attack.

The office oversees sensitive special operations and irregular warfare matters for the Pentagon. The appointment places a convicted rioter from the Capitol attack in a role dealing with counterterrorism and defense policy.

cards.headline: US jet disables oil tanker bound for Iran after vessel ignores blockade warnings
cards.teaser: A fighter jet fired a missile at a tanker headed to an Iranian port after the ship failed to comply with naval blockade orders.
cards.body:
A U.S. fighter jet fired a Hellfire missile that disabled an oil tanker traveling to Iran's Kharg Island port after the vessel ignored repeated warnings, U.S. Central Command announced. The Botswana-flagged M/T Lexie did not comply with directions issued under a U.S. naval maritime blockade.

Centcom said it enforced blockade measures against the tanker. The strike disabled the vessel, preventing it from reaching the Iranian port facility at Kharg Island, a major oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf.

cards.headline: Rubio faces questions over Ebola outbreak response and global health cuts
cards.teaser: Democrats criticized the secretary of state over the administration's reductions to international health programs during an outbreak in Africa.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio faced criticism from Democrats during Capitol Hill hearings on Tuesday regarding the Trump administration's cuts to global health programs and their impact on Ebola response efforts in Africa.

The budget hearings focused on how reduced funding has affected U.S. international disease response capabilities as the Ebola outbreak continues across African nations.

cards.headline: Rep. Tom Kean Jr. to disclose medical condition after three-month absence
cards.teaser: The New Jersey congressman said he will explain his absence from Congress and transition back to work in the coming weeks.
cards.body:
Rep. Tom Kean Jr. said he will reveal his medical condition in a matter of weeks after receiving a reelection endorsement from President Trump. The New Jersey Republican has not voted in Congress since March 5, according to House records.

Kean, son of former New Jersey Gov. Tom Kean, described himself as "energized" and said he will soon transition back to his duties. He faces no opposition in the Republican primary.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner meets with Democrats amid scandal
cards.teaser: The Democratic candidate faced questions from Senate colleagues after reports emerged of sexual text messages.
cards.body:
Democratic Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner met with Senate Democrats in Washington as he seeks to address multiple scandals affecting his campaign to flip a Republican-held seat. Fresh scrutiny emerged after reports surfaced that Platner sent sexual text messages.

Platner is working to shore up support among Senate Democrats for his bid in a race long considered a top target for the party. The meeting comes as he faces a wave of controversies that threaten his campaign.

cards.headline: California governor primary underway with Porter, Steyer, Becerra competing
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer and Xavier Becerra face Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton to replace Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California's governor primary is underway with Democrats and Republicans competing to replace term-limited Gov. Gavin Newsom. On the Democratic side, Xavier Becerra represents the establishment favorite, while Tom Steyer and Katie Porter offer alternative visions for the state's future.

The race reflects a crucial moment for California Democrats, with the outcome potentially shaping the direction of the party in the nation's fourth-largest economy. Results are being tallied as voting concludes across the state.
